evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Arden: 'in order for us to put together an estimate, I have to ask some few questions that might take around ten to fifteen minutes. Would that be fine?' — asked but immediately pivots to agenda without waiting for a clear yes before continuing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Arden: 'before we go over that estimate or before we discuss that other than price or are there any biggest concerns or questions about the move that you would want answers within this call?' — asked, but this comes after already starting probing (already confirmed two-bedroom apartment, unit number, square footage exploration).
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer stated 'No ma'am' to concerns, no concerns raised to follow up on.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised, nothing to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Arden gathered property type (2-bed apartment to 4-bed house, 1-story), floor/stories (second floor apartment with staircase access), number of rooms (confirmed), walking distance (parking confirmed in same driveway), additional rooms (balcony with plants, not moving), special considerations (60-inch TV, washer/dryer, one bed), additional stops (none mentioned). All seven logistics categories covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Arden: 'Do you need help packing though or everything will be packed once we get there?' — Customer declined.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Arden: 'typically for a two bedroom apartment box count has been $25 to 35 how many number or how many maximum total' — box count range given and customer confirmed approximately the same.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Arden: 'typically a two bedroom apartment usually takes two movers between four and a half to six and a half hours... in your case since we're going to be moving you from the second floor... I'm estimating the move to take only around four and a half to five and a half hours... $934 to $1,126' — range anchored to typical two-bedroom plus personalized to second-floor staircase access and special items (TVs).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Arden: '$192 per hour for two movers, 26 foot box truck... gas trucks, taxes, insurance, all the wraps, the pads and bans... there's gonna be no hidden fee, no credit card fee, no terrible fees' and 'two and a half hour minimum once we go over the minimum the time will be prorated in fifteen minutes. Increment.' Full fee transparency and 2.5-hour minimum/15-minute-increment framing delivered.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: After estimate quote ($934–$1,126), customer asked 'can we get that in writing?' Rep responded with sending email quote, never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or gave silence.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Arden: 'you also have an on time guarantee. So, if the movers arrive late you start ticket discount on your final bill' — discount terms for lateness stated, framing present as 'start discount' (immediately discounting).
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Arden: 'you're also gonna get up to $2,000 free evaluation coverage so if anything gets damage gets broken or gets mis during the move... we're either gonna repair or replace and reimburse zero deductible and that's gonna be handled within three to five business days' — $2,000 coverage, zero deductible, no fine-print framing explicitly stated, built into rate implied by context.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No closing question like 'Does that put those to rest?' asked after Two Promises delivery. Rep moved directly into estimate discussion.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: After pricing and promises, rep asked 'Before we go over pricing structure and estimate, do you have any questions, any clarification regarding the moving process in general?' This occurs mid-call, not as a final check near the ask. No genuine 'What's still concerning you?' asked near the end.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar catch-all asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Arden never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any explicit ask for the business. Call ends with rep saying 'once you're ready to book you just have to give us a call' and 'stay safe and enjoy the rest of your day. Bye-bye.' — customer booking status unclear, no direct ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Arden: 'securing a slot does not require any deposit, okay? And just in case you would need rescheduling that's gonna be free of cost as well' — no deposit framing present early in call.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial — date confirmed (Thursday October 8th), no phone number collected, arrival window not confirmed, crew size (two movers) mentioned in estimate context but not explicitly confirmed as part of booking, addresses mentioned (origin and destination) but not re-confirmed as booking detail, no crew notes about customer concerns left.

top_strength: Arden gathered comprehensive logistics details across all seven categories and delivered both promises (On-Time Guarantee and Damage Coverage) with clear, specific terms, building strong credibility around coverage and protections.
coaching_note: Never ask for the business explicitly — the call ends without a direct 'Would you like our help with your move?' and no actual booking is confirmed; add a genuine final concerns check and close the Two Promises section before moving to estimate, and always pause after 'Does that feel fair?' to let the customer respond.
booking_note: Customer asked for quote in writing to compare with other companies but made no explicit commitment to book. Salesman said 'once you're ready to book you just have to give us a call' indicating no booking was confirmed on this call.
